headline: Scientific inquiry asks questions nature must answer—through observation and experiment
universal_truth: The universe doesn't lie; ask the right questions and observe carefully, and reality will teach you
fun_facts: The scientific method has only existed for about 400 years—before that, knowledge was often just authority
Science advances by falsification—proving old ideas wrong, not just confirming them
Peer review means scientists check each other's work before it's published
discussion_questions: How do you investigate questions when you don't know the answer?
What would a 'scientific approach' look like in your daily decisions?
How do you distinguish between what you've tested and what you've assumed?

hook.script: Before science, we asked authorities. Now we ask nature directly—through observation and experiment. The universe doesn't lie, doesn't have opinions, doesn't play favorites. Ask the right questions, and reality will answer.

cliff.script: Science transformed our world by changing how we get knowledge. What's special about scientific inquiry?

options.text: Science forces reality to answer—it doesn't rely on authority, tradition, or intuition alone; it tests ideas against nature, and nature doesn't lie; wrong ideas get exposed
options.response: Yes. Science is humble before reality. Ideas must face evidence. Wrong ideas get corrected. It's a self-correcting system that converges on truth over time.
True, but the method—testing against reality—is what makes those facts reliable...

fact1.title: Question Formulation
fact1.script: Good science starts with good questions—specific enough to test, open enough to surprise. 'How does this work?' 'What would happen if?' The question frames the investigation.

fact2.title: Controlled Testing
fact2.script: Experiments control variables to isolate causes. Change one thing, keep others constant, observe what happens. This reveals causation, not just correlation.

fact3.title: Personal Science
fact3.script: You can apply scientific thinking personally: ask clear questions, make predictions, test against reality, update based on results. Reality will teach you—if you let it.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: The universe doesn't lie. Ask the right questions and observe carefully, and reality will teach you. Be a scientist of your own life.

outro.script: That's Day 296. Tomorrow, we'll explore seeing on purpose—observation. Until then, formulate a question and let reality answer.

growTrack.title: Personal Experiment - What Can Reality Teach You?
growTrack.learning_objective: Apply scientific inquiry to personal questions
growTrack.activity: Pick a question about your life you don't know the answer to. Formulate it clearly. What test or observation would give you an answer? Design a small experiment and let reality teach you.
